title: GitHub - ehnruiz/claude-skills: Claude Code skills, subagents and hooks for an agent that proves its work.
excerpt: Claude Code skills, subagents and hooks for an agent that proves its work. - ehnruiz/claude-skills
content_html:
Skills, subagents and hooks for Claude Code, for engineers who want an agent that proves its work. A supervisor sends each step to the cheapest model that can do it and moves it up a tier after two failures. A gate passes by its exit code. A bug fix ships with a test shown to fail without the fix, and a session ends with a handoff note the next one picks up. The library checks itself: frontmatter, links, scripts, hooks and this README run in CI, and a collision audit keeps skill descriptions from competing.

The regression-proof skill on a real fix from this repository: the new test fails on the code from before the fix and passes with it, so it proves the fix. The recording is shortened: it skips the step that lists which test files the fix changed, and shows only the result lines of each run. docs/examples.md has the full recipe.

Install

As a plugin, from inside Claude Code:

/plugin marketplace add ehnruiz/claude-skills
/plugin install agent-workflow@ehnruiz

The plugin is agent-workflow in the ehnruiz marketplace, the names in .claude-plugin/. Once installed, its skills are namespaced: /agent-workflow:handoff, /agent-workflow:pick-up. The same two steps from a shell are claude plugin marketplace add ehnruiz/claude-skills and claude plugin install agent-workflow@ehnruiz, and claude plugin list then shows agent-workflow@ehnruiz with its version.

With the skills CLI, which can also install into other coding agents (--agent):

npx skills add ehnruiz/claude-skills              # pick from the list
npx skills add ehnruiz/claude-skills --skill tdd  # one skill

Or copy only the parts you want:

git clone https://github.com/ehnruiz/claude-skills
cp -R claude-skills/skills/ticket-write ~/.claude/skills/
cp claude-skills/agents/*.md ~/.claude/agents/

Requirements (Claude Code; Python 3.9+ for the scripts and the SessionStart hook; Node 20+ for the opt-in hooks), what was tested where, and how to check each install path are in docs/install.md.

Quick start

After the plugin install, claude plugin list shows agent-workflow@ehnruiz as enabled. Two of the scripts run without a model, so from a clone they are a quick check that Python and the paths are right:

$ python3 hooks/handoff_notice.py --print-dir
/Users/you/.claude/projects/-Users-you-projects-claude-skills/handoffs
$ python3 skills/skill-collision-audit/scripts/find_collisions.py skills
22 skills, 1 overlapping pairs, 0 duplicate names
...

Then the workflow the skills are built around, on a project of yours. The slash commands assume the plugin install; with a copy install drop the agent-workflow: prefix.

  1. Start the session and say what is wrong. "The date parser drops the timezone on 2026-10-16T09:00+02:00. Diagnose it and fix it." The diagnosing-bugs skill fires on "diagnose": it builds a command that goes red on the bug before anyone guesses at a cause, then reproduces, ranks hypotheses and instruments one variable at a time.
  2. Let the supervisor route the steps. With more than one step, supervisor fires. It keeps the plan and the judgment in your session, sends a Haiku scout to find the parser and its tests, and hands the fix to a Sonnet implementer as one ticket: the behavior wanted, where it goes, the command that proves it, the files involved, what must stay unchanged. The tdd skill makes the implementer write the failing test first. A worker that fails the same ticket twice moves up a tier with its failed report attached.
  3. Read the gates as exit codes. The supervisor runs lint, the type check and the tests itself, one command per step, and reports lint=0 typecheck=0 test=0, never "all green". The regression-proof skill adds the step most people skip: in a scratch worktree at the merge base, with only the new test copied in, the test must fail. docs/examples.md shows that recipe on a real fix from this repository, with both exit codes.
  4. Send the diff to review. The Opus reviewer reads the diff against the ask and the project's standards and reports each finding with a file, a line and a failure scenario. The supervisor fixes what holds up and reruns the gates.
  5. Stop without losing the thread. /agent-workflow:handoff writes a note outside the repository: goal, what is done and how it was verified, decisions, open questions, next steps. The next session sees the opening of that note at startup through the handoff_notice.py hook, and /agent-workflow:pick-up checks the repository for drift before it starts on the next step.

The prompts in steps 1 and 2 show the shape of a request; no session was run against them for this page. What was run is the scripts, the hooks, the tests and the install path, and docs/install.md says where.

Examples

Three examples run against this repository, with the commands and the exit codes that came back, are in docs/examples.md:

  • regression-proof applied to commit 356016b: the new test fails on the parent commit (exit 1) and passes on the fix (exit 0), the verdict a pull request's test plan should carry.
  • skill-collision-audit on this repository's 21 skills: one pair flagged at 0.32, judged resolved because each description names the other and draws the line.
  • supervisor on the pull request that added the docs: what stayed with the supervisor and why, what was delegated to which tier, what the review found, and the gates with their exit codes.

Skills

Skill What it does
supervisor Splits a multi-step task into tickets for cheaper subagents, in a fixed order: clarify, scout, plan, build, verify, review, ship. A subagent that fails twice moves up one model tier.
grilling Questions you about a plan in rounds until every decision is settled. It looks up facts itself and asks you only for decisions.
tdd Test-driven development, one vertical slice at a time: what a good test is, where tests go, when to mock, and the rules of the red-green loop.
diagnosing-bugs For hard bugs, flaky tests and slowdowns: build a command that goes red on the bug first, then reproduce, rank hypotheses, instrument, fix behind a test and clean up.
regression-proof Judges lint, type checks, tests and pushes by their exit codes, and proves in a scratch worktree that a fix's new test fails without the fix.
explain-the-number Before a measured number is reported or credited to a change, checks the comparison is like-for-like: same population, same measures, same setup, nothing else changed. What did not run is reported as "did not run".
research Answers a question from primary sources in one cited Markdown note, written in the background by researcher.
writing-for-agents How to write skills, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md so an agent follows them the same way every run, and how to prove a new rule red then green in fresh subagents before it ships.
retro Reviews a finished session for what slowed the agent down or let a mistake through, then turns one lesson into a test, check or doc in the project. You invoke it yourself.
handoff Writes a handoff note at the end of a session: the goal, what is done and how it was verified, decisions, open questions and next steps. You invoke it yourself.
pick-up Loads the newest handoff, checks the repository for anything that changed since, and starts on the next step.
no-ai-attribution Removes AI credit lines and AI co-author trailers from commits, PRs, issues, comments and tickets before they are posted.
open-in-my-browser Opens links you share in your own Chrome through the Claude in Chrome extension, so pages behind your sign-ins and VPN load.
ticket-write Drafts bugs, tasks, stories, spikes and epics with word budgets, then checks the draft with a lint script before filing. Works with Jira, Linear or GitHub Issues.
ticket-trim Shortens an existing ticket that is too long. It saves the original text in a comment first.
ticket-digest Turns today's new tickets into one message to paste into chat, one line per ticket.
llm-integration A checklist for code that calls a language model or exposes tools to one: prompts as versioned source, model output as untrusted input, cost caps, and how an MCP server should stop.
plain-writing Drafts messages, emails, PR descriptions and comments in plain language under your name, and cuts the patterns that read as machine-written. Tickets go to ticket-write and ticket-trim.
epic-review Checks a Jira epic item by item against its In Scope list, flags what the review meeting must decide, and drafts the scope of the next epic.
confluence-jira-links Shows each ticket on a Confluence page as a smart link and makes sure each ticket links back to the page once, not twice.
leader-1-1-prep Builds a one-screen brief for a 1:1 with a skip-level: what carried forward, at most two asks, people, strategy, and one question about your growth.
skill-collision-audit Finds skills whose descriptions compete for the same request, then fixes the descriptions so each request goes to exactly one skill. A script shortlists the overlapping pairs and same-name duplicates; Claude judges each pair against realistic requests.

Ticket budgets

Part Ceiling
Title 80 characters
Description (bug, task, story) 150 words
Description (spike, epic) 80 words
Acceptance criteria 2 to 5 bullets
Code identifiers in the description 3
Technical notes comment 250 words

skills/ticket-write/scripts/ticket_lint.py checks a draft against these limits and lists the identifiers that should move to the technical notes:

$ python3 ticket_lint.py --type bug --title "Product pages lose search data" draft.md
ok    title characters: 30 (limit 80)
ok    description words: 36 (limit 150)
ok    headings: 3 (limit 6)
ok    code identifiers: 0 (limit 3)
ok    acceptance criteria: 2 (limit 2-5)

Collision audit

skills/skill-collision-audit/scripts/find_collisions.py scores every pair of skill descriptions by the distinctive words they share:

$ python3 find_collisions.py ~/.claude/skills .claude/skills
55 skills, 14 overlapping pairs, 0 duplicate names

0.73  built-in-browser  <->  chrome-browser
      shared: browser, tool, mcp, chrome, own, before

A high score is a reason to look, not a verdict: that pair already says in both descriptions which browser each one is for. The skill has Claude test each pair with realistic requests and fix only the real collisions.

Subagents

Each subagent's model is set in its file. The supervisor skill sends work to them.

Agent Model Job
scout Haiku Finds things and returns file:line pointers. It changes nothing.
doc-writer Haiku Writes prose from the facts it is given, and writes TODO(fact) where a fact is missing.
implementer Sonnet Builds one ticket test-first and reports each command's exit code. It does not commit.
tester Sonnet Writes and runs tests, and touches only tests and fixtures.
researcher Sonnet Reads primary sources in the background and writes a note where every claim has a source and a date.
reviewer Opus Reviews a diff against the ticket and the repository's standards, giving a failure scenario for each finding.

Hooks

Hook Event What it does
handoff_notice.py SessionStart Shows the opening of the project's newest handoff note when a session starts, and names pick-up. Quiet when there is no note, or when the repository has its own handoff skill.
config-protection.mjs PreToolUse Opt-in. Blocks edits to an existing lint, type, test, build or CI configuration file.
commit-secrets.mjs PreToolUse Opt-in. Scans what a git commit would take and denies or asks when it finds a secret.
git-guardrails.mjs PreToolUse Opt-in. Blocks git push, git reset --hard, git clean and git branch -D before they run.
edited-files.mjs PostToolUse Opt-in. Records the files a session edits, for stop-check.mjs.
stop-check.mjs Stop Opt-in. Runs eslint and the type check on the edited files before a response ends.

The plugin registers handoff_notice.py through hooks/hooks.json. The five opt-in hooks are not registered: hooks/README.md has the settings snippet for them. With a copy install, add handoff_notice.py to ~/.claude/settings.json:

{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      { "matcher": "startup|clear|compact",
        "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "python3 /path/to/claude-skills/hooks/handoff_notice.py", "timeout": 10 }] }
    ]
  }
}

Rules for your CLAUDE.md

Some habits depend on a moment in the session rather than on a request, so a skill description never fires for them. Put them in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md instead.

File a waiting session in the desktop app. In the Claude desktop app, create a sidebar section named "Pending my feedback", then add:

Whenever a session ends its turn waiting on my answer, decision or approval, move it into the sidebar
section named "Pending my feedback" (`mcp__ccd_sidebar__move_sessions` with `session_ids: ["self"]` and the
section's id from `mcp__ccd_sidebar__list_sections`; load the tools with ToolSearch first if they are
deferred). Once I have answered and the work resumes, move it back to Ungrouped (`section_id: "sessions"`)
or to the section it came from. Sessions outside the desktop app skip this.

Your own copy wins

A skill in ~/.claude/skills/ outranks a project's .claude/skills/ skill with the same name. So supervisor, handoff, pick-up, tdd and diagnosing-bugs each check first for a project copy and follow that one when it exists. Subagents need no such step: a project's .claude/agents/ file already outranks the one installed here.

Development

python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
node --test tests/hooks/
claude plugin validate .

The Node tests cover the five opt-in hooks. The Python tests check the lint script, the collision script, the handoff hook, each skill's and subagent's frontmatter, links inside the skills and the docs, that this README lists every skill and subagent and names the plugin as the manifests do, and that the changelog has a section for the current version. CI runs both suites on the oldest and the current supported runtimes: Python 3.9 and 3.12, Node 20 and 22.

Releases

CHANGELOG.md lists what each version changed. docs/releasing.md says when the version is bumped, how a release is tagged and how installed users receive it.

Credits

The handoff skill grew out of the handoff idea in Matt Pocock's skills. grilling, tdd, diagnosing-bugs, research, writing-for-agents and retro are adapted from the same repository under the MIT License; each keeps the notice in its own LICENSE.md. The git-guardrails.mjs hook is adapted from its git-guardrails-claude-code skill, with the credit in the hook's header comment.

explain-the-number follows the principle of the same name in Lauren Tan's pstack (MIT); it keeps the notice in its own LICENSE.md. writing-for-agents/PRESSURE-TESTS.md rewrites the method of Jesse Vincent's testing-skills-with-subagents in obra/clank; no text is copied, as that repository ships no license file.

License

MIT

content_html_zh:
Skills, subagents and hooks for Claude Code, for engineers who want an agent that proves its work. A supervisor sends each step to the cheapest model that can do it and moves it up a tier after two failures. A gate passes by its exit code. A bug fix ships with a test shown to fail without the fix, and a session ends with a handoff note the next one picks up. The library checks itself: frontmatter, links, scripts, hooks and this README run in CI, and a collision audit keeps skill descriptions from competing.

The regression-proof skill on a real fix from this repository: the new test fails on the code from before the fix and passes with it, so it proves the fix. The recording is shortened: it skips the step that lists which test files the fix changed, and shows only the result lines of each run. docs/examples.md has the full recipe.

安装

As a plugin, from inside Claude Code:

/plugin marketplace add ehnruiz/claude-skills
/plugin install agent-workflow@ehnruiz

The plugin is agent-workflow in the ehnruiz marketplace, the names in .claude-plugin/. Once installed, its skills are namespaced: /agent-workflow:handoff, /agent-workflow:pick-up. The same two steps from a shell are claude plugin marketplace add ehnruiz/claude-skills and claude plugin install agent-workflow@ehnruiz, and claude plugin list then shows agent-workflow@ehnruiz with its version.

With the skills CLI, which can also install into other coding agents (--agent):

npx skills add ehnruiz/claude-skills              # pick from the list
npx skills add ehnruiz/claude-skills --skill tdd  # one skill

Or copy only the parts you want:

git clone https://github.com/ehnruiz/claude-skills
cp -R claude-skills/skills/ticket-write ~/.claude/skills/
cp claude-skills/agents/*.md ~/.claude/agents/

Requirements (Claude Code; Python 3.9+ for the scripts and the SessionStart hook; Node 20+ for the opt-in hooks), what was tested where, and how to check each install path are in docs/install.md.

快速启动

After the plugin install, claude plugin list shows agent-workflow@ehnruiz as enabled. Two of the scripts run without a model, so from a clone they are a quick check that Python and the paths are right:

$ python3 hooks/handoff_notice.py --print-dir
/Users/you/.claude/projects/-Users-you-projects-claude-skills/handoffs
$ python3 skills/skill-collision-audit/scripts/find_collisions.py skills
22 skills, 1 overlapping pairs, 0 duplicate names
...

Then the workflow the skills are built around, on a project of yours. The slash commands assume the plugin install; with a copy install drop the agent-workflow: prefix.

  1. Start the session and say what is wrong. "The date parser drops the timezone on 2026-10-16T09:00+02:00. Diagnose it and fix it." The diagnosing-bugs skill fires on "diagnose": it builds a command that goes red on the bug before anyone guesses at a cause, then reproduces, ranks hypotheses and instruments one variable at a time.
  2. Let the supervisor route the steps. With more than one step, supervisor fires. It keeps the plan and the judgment in your session, sends a Haiku scout to find the parser and its tests, and hands the fix to a Sonnet implementer as one ticket: the behavior wanted, where it goes, the command that proves it, the files involved, what must stay unchanged. The tdd skill makes the implementer write the failing test first. A worker that fails the same ticket twice moves up a tier with its failed report attached.
  3. Read the gates as exit codes. The supervisor runs lint, the type check and the tests itself, one command per step, and reports lint=0 typecheck=0 test=0, never "all green". The regression-proof skill adds the step most people skip: in a scratch worktree at the merge base, with only the new test copied in, the test must fail. docs/examples.md shows that recipe on a real fix from this repository, with both exit codes.
  4. Send the diff to review. The Opus reviewer reads the diff against the ask and the project's standards and reports each finding with a file, a line and a failure scenario. The supervisor fixes what holds up and reruns the gates.
  5. Stop without losing the thread. /agent-workflow:handoff writes a note outside the repository: goal, what is done and how it was verified, decisions, open questions, next steps. The next session sees the opening of that note at startup through the handoff_notice.py hook, and /agent-workflow:pick-up checks the repository for drift before it starts on the next step.

The prompts in steps 1 and 2 show the shape of a request; no session was run against them for this page. What was run is the scripts, the hooks, the tests and the install path, and docs/install.md says where.

示例

Three examples run against this repository, with the commands and the exit codes that came back, are in docs/examples.md:

  • regression-proof applied to commit 356016b: the new test fails on the parent commit (exit 1) and passes on the fix (exit 0), the verdict a pull request's test plan should carry.
  • skill-collision-audit on this repository's 21 skills: one pair flagged at 0.32, judged resolved because each description names the other and draws the line.
  • supervisor on the pull request that added the docs: what stayed with the supervisor and why, what was delegated to which tier, what the review found, and the gates with their exit codes.

grilling Questions you about a plan in rounds until every decision is settled. It looks up facts itself and asks you only for decisions.
tdd Test-driven development, one vertical slice at a time: what a good test is, where tests go, when to mock, and the rules of the red-green loop.
diagnosing-bugs For hard bugs, flaky tests and slowdowns: build a command that goes red on the bug first, then reproduce, rank hypotheses, instrument, fix behind a test and clean up.
regression-proof Judges lint, type checks, tests and pushes by their exit codes, and proves in a scratch worktree that a fix's new test fails without the fix.
explain-the-number Before a measured number is reported or credited to a change, checks the comparison is like-for-like: same population, same measures, same setup, nothing else changed. What did not run is reported as "did not run".
research Answers a question from primary sources in one cited Markdown note, written in the background by researcher.
writing-for-agents How to write skills, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md so an agent follows them the same way every run, and how to prove a new rule red then green in fresh subagents before it ships.
retro Reviews a finished session for what slowed the agent down or let a mistake through, then turns one lesson into a test, check or doc in the project. You invoke it yourself.
不可触摸 Writes a handoff note at the end of a session: the goal, what is done and how it was verified, decisions, open questions and next steps. You invoke it yourself.
pick-up Loads the newest handoff, checks the repository for anything that changed since, and starts on the next step.
no-ai-attribution Removes AI credit lines and AI co-author trailers from commits, PRs, issues, comments and tickets before they are posted.
open-in-my-browser Opens links you share in your own Chrome through the Claude in Chrome extension, so pages behind your sign-ins and VPN load.
ticket-write Drafts bugs, tasks, stories, spikes and epics with word budgets, then checks the draft with a lint script before filing. Works with Jira, Linear or GitHub Issues.
ticket-trim Shortens an existing ticket that is too long. It saves the original text in a comment first.
ticket-digest Turns today's new tickets into one message to paste into chat, one line per ticket.
llm-integration A checklist for code that calls a language model or exposes tools to one: prompts as versioned source, model output as untrusted input, cost caps, and how an MCP server should stop.
plain-writing Drafts messages, emails, PR descriptions and comments in plain language under your name, and cuts the patterns that read as machine-written. Tickets go to ticket-write and ticket-trim.
epic-review Checks a Jira epic item by item against its In Scope list, flags what the review meeting must decide, and drafts the scope of the next epic.
confluence-jira-links Shows each ticket on a Confluence page as a smart link and makes sure each ticket links back to the page once, not twice.
leader-1-1-prep Builds a one-screen brief for a 1:1 with a skip-level: what carried forward, at most two asks, people, strategy, and one question about your growth.
skill-collision-audit Finds skills whose descriptions compete for the same request, then fixes the descriptions so each request goes to exactly one skill. A script shortlists the overlapping pairs and same-name duplicates; Claude judges each pair against realistic requests.

Ticket budgets

Part Ceiling
Title 80 characters
Description (bug, task, story) 150 words
Description (spike, epic) 80 words
Acceptance criteria 2 to 5 bullets
Code identifiers in the description 3
Technical notes comment 250 words

skills/ticket-write/scripts/ticket_lint.py checks a draft against these limits and lists the identifiers that should move to the technical notes:

$ python3 ticket_lint.py --type bug --title "Product pages lose search data" draft.md
ok    title characters: 30 (limit 80)
ok    description words: 36 (limit 150)
ok    headings: 3 (limit 6)
ok    code identifiers: 0 (limit 3)
ok    acceptance criteria: 2 (limit 2-5)

Collision audit

skills/skill-collision-audit/scripts/find_collisions.py scores every pair of skill descriptions by the distinctive words they share:

$ python3 find_collisions.py ~/.claude/skills .claude/skills
55 skills, 14 overlapping pairs, 0 duplicate names

0.73  built-in-browser  <->  chrome-browser
      shared: browser, tool, mcp, chrome, own, before

A high score is a reason to look, not a verdict: that pair already says in both descriptions which browser each one is for. The skill has Claude test each pair with realistic requests and fix only the real collisions.

子代理

Each subagent's model is set in its file. The supervisor skill sends work to them.

Agent Model Job
scout Haiku Finds things and returns file:line pointers. It changes nothing.
doc-writer Haiku Writes prose from the facts it is given, and writes TODO(fact) where a fact is missing.
implementer Sonnet Builds one ticket test-first and reports each command's exit code. It does not commit.
tester Sonnet Writes and runs tests, and touches only tests and fixtures.
researcher Sonnet Reads primary sources in the background and writes a note where every claim has a source and a date.
reviewer Opus Reviews a diff against the ticket and the repository's standards, giving a failure scenario for each finding.

Hooks

Hook Event 它的作用
handoff_notice.py 会话开始 Shows the opening of the project's newest handoff note when a session starts, and names pick-up. Quiet when there is no note, or when the repository has its own handoff skill.
config-protection.mjs 预工具使用 Opt-in. Blocks edits to an existing lint, type, test, build or CI configuration file.
commit-secrets.mjs 预工具使用 Opt-in. Scans what a git commit would take and denies or asks when it finds a secret.
git-guardrails.mjs 预工具使用 Opt-in. Blocks git push, git reset --hard, git clean and git branch -D before they run.
edited-files.mjs 后期工具使用 Opt-in. Records the files a session edits, for stop-check.mjs.
stop-check.mjs Stop Opt-in. Runs eslint and the type check on the edited files before a response ends.

The plugin registers handoff_notice.py through hooks/hooks.json. The five opt-in hooks are not registered: hooks/README.md has the settings snippet for them. With a copy install, add handoff_notice.py to ~/.claude/settings.json:

{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      { "matcher": "startup|clear|compact",
        "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "python3 /path/to/claude-skills/hooks/handoff_notice.py", "timeout": 10 }] }
    ]
  }
}

Rules for your CLAUDE.md

Some habits depend on a moment in the session rather than on a request, so a skill description never fires for them. Put them in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md instead.

File a waiting session in the desktop app. In the Claude desktop app, create a sidebar section named "Pending my feedback", then add:

Whenever a session ends its turn waiting on my answer, decision or approval, move it into the sidebar
section named "Pending my feedback" (`mcp__ccd_sidebar__move_sessions` with `session_ids: ["self"]` and the
section's id from `mcp__ccd_sidebar__list_sections`; load the tools with ToolSearch first if they are
deferred). Once I have answered and the work resumes, move it back to Ungrouped (`section_id: "sessions"`)
or to the section it came from. Sessions outside the desktop app skip this.

Your own copy wins

A skill in ~/.claude/skills/ outranks a project's .claude/skills/ skill with the same name. So supervisor, handoff, pick-up, tdd and diagnosing-bugs each check first for a project copy and follow that one when it exists. Subagents need no such step: a project's .claude/agents/ file already outranks the one installed here.

发展

python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
node --test tests/hooks/
claude plugin validate .

The Node tests cover the five opt-in hooks. The Python tests check the lint script, the collision script, the handoff hook, each skill's and subagent's frontmatter, links inside the skills and the docs, that this README lists every skill and subagent and names the plugin as the manifests do, and that the changelog has a section for the current version. CI runs both suites on the oldest and the current supported runtimes: Python 3.9 and 3.12, Node 20 and 22.

发布

CHANGELOG.md lists what each version changed. docs/releasing.md says when the version is bumped, how a release is tagged and how installed users receive it.
